Plankton.et: Derived from Ancient Greek πλαγκτός (planktós, “drifter”), from πλάζω (plázō, “I turn aside, wander”). Coined by German zoologist Victor Hensen in 1887.

Plasma.et: From Late Latin plasma (literally “mold”), from Ancient Greek πλάσμα (plásma, “something formed”).

Plunder.et: From Middle High German plunder (“household furniture, clothes, linen”). Cognate with Middle Low German plunde (“clothing”), Dutch plunderen (“to plunder”).

Plural.et: From German Pluralis, from Latin (numerus) plūrālis.

Plutonium.et: Borrowed from English plutonium, hence from Pluto in the sense of the dwarf planet.

Platin.et: Borrowed from French platine, from Spanish platina.
